title: [Platform] Jira Bug and Temporal schedule triggers for routines
goal: Start bug fixers from triaged Bug tickets through the Jira poll that already exists, and start the scheduled routines and housekeeping jobs from Temporal schedules at odd minutes in Israel time, with no new public webhook.
outcome: In the Temporal UI's Schedules page you see sched:<name> for each scheduled job whose code has merged (daily ones Sunday to Thursday in Asia/Jerusalem time), plus poll-jira-bugfix-fe and poll-jira-bugfix-be every 5 minutes once Security has named its label. A Bug in RH that is in To Do, unassigned and labelled FE starts bugfix:RH-<n> on ai-agents-bugfix, and a second poll does nothing new. When a person assigns that bug to themselves, its run stops within about 5 minutes.

dependsOn.why: Listed dependency: routineRun with its stop signal, CHARTER_SHA, and agentFor.
Listed dependency: the trigger side is in place and the bugfix:<key> and sched:<name> ID rules are agreed.
The Jira query registry (QUERIES), ensureSchedules, the Jira client, and schedules.ts itself. G4-04 changed toStart to an async function that may skip a match.
startRun gives every bug run the ID bugfix:<key> on ai-agents-bugfix, so a repeat poll is a no-op; agentAttribute tags scheduled routine runs.
The guilds' answer on how a Bug counts as triaged into a team (proposal: the label FE or BE).

access.what: Write access to RhinoHealth/ai-agents and one approval.
The label that keeps a ticket away from agents when it might hold customer data.
The Nova Jira service account can browse Bugs in project RH (the poll runs the JQL as Nova).
access.who: A Jira site admin (G4-04 created the account).

decide.q: Which label keeps a Bug away from agents because it might hold customer data?
decide.fallback: Do not register the bug queries at all: registerBugQueries is not called and no Bug reaches an agent. The schedules still land. PHI never enters a prompt, so "no answer" must mean "off".

decide.q: How does a Bug count as triaged into a team?
decide.fallback: The label FE or BE on a Bug in To Do, as G5-07 proposes.

decide.q: When a person takes the bug, should the run also post what it found and move the ticket?
decide.fallback: The run ends as stopped and keeps its branch and notes; posting a summary comes with G5-27.

decide.q: G5-30 says the flaky-test tickets are "picked up by the G5-13 poller", but G5-13 registers no such query. Who adds it?
decide.fallback: G5-30 registers its own query in QUERIES the same way, with its own ID rule (flaky:fcp:<hash>).

files.what: The bug query and its registration in G3-28's registry. Each match starts routineRun through startRun as bugfix:<key> on ai-agents-bugfix, so polling again every 5 minutes never starts a second run.

notes.text: Anyone can opt a bug out with no-routine. Values are quoted because JQL treats a dash as special.
Called at worker start only once the customer-data label exists (see the decisions).
Async, as G4-04 changed G3-28's registry; the sketch returned a plain array.

files.what: G5's part of the file G3-28 created: the cron table and ensureCronSchedules(), which creates each schedule or updates it when it exists. An entry whose workflow or charter has not merged yet is skipped, so each owning ticket only has to export its workflow (or add its charter) and the schedule appears on the next deploy.

notes.text: Workflow names are strings, so this file compiles before G5-02, G5-03, G5-15, G5-16 and G5-31 exist.
04:17 Sunday to Thursday, Israel time (0-4 = Sunday-Thursday). The same cron as G5-31.
Not in the sketch: the bug JQL drops assigned tickets, so the poll can never see that a person took one. This sweep can.
Routines run on their family's queue (fe-dead-code on ai-agents-health); housekeeping on ai-agents-orchestrator.
Every deploy updates the schedule, so scheduled runs always use the charter of the code that is running.
Schedules start runs without startRun, so they must set Agent themselves, or the kill switch's batch stop cannot find them.
Not in the sketch: after an outage, do not replay a backlog of missed days (G3-28 does the same for the Jira polls).

files.what: stopTakenBugs: lists running bug-fixer runs, asks Jira which of their tickets now have an assignee, and sends each of those runs the stop signal with the person who assigned it.

notes.text: A visibility query: Temporal's list of runs filtered by type, the Agent attribute and status.
Bug fixers are never assigned the ticket, so any assignee is a person who took it.
Who assigned it, from the changelog, the same way G4-04 finds the requester.

files.what: The tiny workflow the sched:bugfix-taken schedule runs every 5 minutes.
Export the new activity and workflow so the worker registers them.
Register the bug queries before ensureSchedules (once Security has answered), then create the cron schedules.

Three tests: the bug JQL has every condition, no schedule runs on the hour or half hour, and ensureCronSchedules run twice on a local dev server updates instead of duplicating. Run against Temporal SDK 1.24.0, all three pass.

steps.do: Update main and make a branch.
steps.cmd: git switch main && git pull && git switch -c g5-13-bug-and-schedule-triggers

steps.do: Check what G3-28 really built: the registry type, ensureSchedules and the Jira client.
steps.see: toStart returns a Promise (G4-04's change). If it still returns a plain array, change bugs.ts to match and note it in the PR.

steps.do: Append the G5-13 block to orchestrator/src/triggers/schedules.ts and add its imports at the top of the file (agentAttribute, agentFor, CHARTER_SHA, and `import * as workflows from "../workflows/index.js"`).
Add activities/bug-taken.ts and workflows/bug-taken-sweep.ts, and export both.
Edit main.ts: ensureSchedules, then ensureCronSchedules. Leave registerBugQueries commented until Security names the label.
Add the test and run it.
steps.see:
ok 1 - the bug query takes only unassigned, triaged bugs and honours both opt-out labels
ok 2 - no schedule runs on the hour or the half hour
ok 3 - ensureCronSchedules is safe to run twice
# pass 3
# fail 0
# fail 0, no lint or type errors.

steps.do: Commit, push and open the PR.
steps.cmd: git add -A && git commit -m "[Platform] G5-13: Jira Bug and schedule triggers for routines" && git push -u origin HEAD && gh pr create --fill

prove.do: Locally: start a dev server that has the ai-agents namespace and the search attributes, then start the worker from your branch in a second terminal.
prove.cmd:
temporal server start-dev --namespace ai-agents --search-attribute Agent=Keyword --search-attribute Routine=Keyword --search-attribute RunKind=Keyword --search-attribute RoutineOutcome=Keyword --search-attribute Stage=Keyword
node --import tsx orchestrator/src/main.ts
prove.see: The worker starts without errors; the Temporal UI (http://localhost:8233, namespace ai-agents) shows the seven slots:<agent> workflows running.

prove.do: List the schedules the worker created.
prove.see: sched:bugfix-taken, plus one sched:<name> for each job whose workflow or charter is already on main.

prove.do: Run one schedule now instead of waiting, and look at the run it started.
prove.cmd:
temporal schedule trigger --namespace ai-agents --schedule-id sched:bugfix-taken
temporal workflow list --namespace ai-agents --query "WorkflowType='bugTakenSweep'" --limit 1
prove.see: Completed  sched:bugfix-taken-<time>  bugTakenSweep  (Temporal adds the time to the ID; seen while writing this card. With no bug runs open, it completes at once with an empty list and never calls Jira.)

prove.do: After deploy and Security's label: label a test Bug FE in To Do, unassigned. Within 5 minutes a run appears; poll again and nothing new appears.
Assign that test Bug to yourself and wait up to 5 minutes.

gaps: The sketch imports noiseSweep, teamDigest, trustLadder and shadowReport, and starts fe-dead-code and kb-ingest, but those workflows and charters come from G5-02, G5-03, G5-15, G5-16, G5-31 and G6-20, which are not dependencies of G5-13. Importing them would break the build. This card names workflows as strings and skips any entry whose workflow is not exported or whose charter does not exist yet.

Schedules start workflows without startRun, so in the sketch scheduled routine runs have no Agent attribute, and the kill switch's batch stop cannot find them. This card sets typedSearchAttributes on routine schedules. routineRun's gate also reads the kill switch, so a stopped agent's scheduled run ends at once.
The sketch calls queueFor(name) with schedule names such as noise-close, which are not routines. This card sends housekeeping to ai-agents-orchestrator and routines to their family's queue.

Temporal adds the scheduled time to the workflow ID of every run a schedule starts (seen on the dev server: sched:bugfix-taken-2026-10-15T17:58:56Z). So sched:<name> in STORY.md's canon is the schedule's ID, not the run's ID, and "one run per thing" for schedules comes from overlap SKIP, not from the ID.
The sketch's toStart returns a plain array, but G3-28's registry (after G4-04's change) expects an async function that may return undefined. This card uses async.
routineRun is started without a charterSha in the sketch (TICKET_ISSUES.md). This card passes CHARTER_SHA; each deploy updates the schedules with the new commit.

The ticket says to stop the run when the assignee changes, but no ticket says who watches for that, and the bug JQL drops assigned tickets, so the poll cannot see it. This card adds the bugfix-taken sweep every 5 minutes. G5-08's sketch also had no stop signal (the G5-08 card adds it).
The "how" says "Weekly code-health routines run on Sunday", but fe-dead-code's cron (here and in G5-31) runs Sunday to Thursday every day. Keep the cron from G5-31 and fix the sentence.
G5-30 says flaky-test tickets are picked up by "the G5-13 poller", but G5-13 registers no flaky query, and the ID flaky:fcp:<hash> appears in neither G3-25's nor G5-09's list of IDs.
The sketch sets no catchupWindow on the cron schedules, so after a long outage Temporal could start missed runs late. This card sets 1 hour, as G3-28 does for the polls.
reconcile.md notes that the Jira poller work is counted three times (G3-28, G4-04, G5-13, about a day). This card only adds registrations to G3-28's mechanism.

Say clearly in the body that the bug queries stay off until Security (Ronen) names the customer-data label, and link that conversation.
List which CRON entries will appear on deploy and which wait for their tickets.

rollback: Revert the PR and redeploy, then delete the schedules this card created, because a revert does not remove schedules from Temporal: for each sched:<name> and poll-jira-bugfix-fe/-be run temporal schedule delete --namespace ai-agents --schedule-id <id>. Bug runs already started can be stopped with the batch stop on Agent="bugfix".
prompt:
You are helping Sean do ticket G5-13 ("Jira Bug and Temporal schedule triggers for routines") in the RhinoHealth/ai-agents repo (TypeScript on Node 24, npm workspaces, ESM with .js import paths, node:test through tsx).

Goal:
1. Bug fixers: register two queries (bugfix-fe, bugfix-be) in G3-28's Jira query registry, every 5 minutes: Bugs in project RH, To Do, unassigned, labelled FE or BE, not labelled no-routine or the customer-data label. Each match starts routineRun through startRun as bugfix:<key> on ai-agents-bugfix.
2. A sweep every 5 minutes that stops a running bug fix when a person has taken the ticket (stop signal).
3. ensureCronSchedules(): Temporal schedules at odd minutes, Asia/Jerusalem, overlap SKIP, created or updated at every worker start.

Start from the card: ~/Projects/ai-agents-course/content/cards/G5-13.json. files[].code.text has tested code for triggers/bugs.ts, the block to append to triggers/schedules.ts, activities/bug-taken.ts, workflows/bug-taken-sweep.ts, the main.ts change and the test. First read what G3-28 really built (schedules.ts, jira.ts) and adapt.

Walls:
- The bug queries stay OFF (registerBugQueries not called) until Security names the customer-data label. PHI never enters a prompt.
- No new public webhook; Jira is only polled.
- Every routine start goes through startRun, or sets the Agent search attribute itself (schedules).
- Do not touch .github/ or protected paths. Do not commit or push; show me the diff.
- If you use subagents, at most two, and tell them not to start their own.

Done when:
1. `node --import tsx --test orchestrator/test/schedules.test.ts` prints "# pass 3" and "# fail 0".
2. `npm run check` is green.
3. You tell me which CRON entries will be created on deploy and which are skipped, and what in the repo did not match the card.
